nodes.name: Electrospinning of precursor solution
nodes.procedure: IrCl₃·xH₂O and Y(NO₃)₃·6H₂O with the desired amounts were dissolved in 700 μL of DMF and 500 μL of ultrapure water, respectively. The total amount of (Ir + Y) was controlled at 4 mmol. Simultaneously, 400 mg of PVP was dissolved in 1.8 mL of DMF under vigorous magnetic stirring for 6 h Subsequently, the IrCl₃·xH₂O solution was dropped into the as-prepared PVP solution. Then, the aqueous Y(NO₃)₃·6H₂O solution was added dropwise with constant agitation for 6 h After thorough mixing, the solution was incubated at room temperature for 2 h and loaded into a plastic syringe. The distance between the plastic syringe needle and aluminum foil was fixed at 15 cm. The electrospinning was performed at a flow rate of 12 μL min⁻¹ under an applied electric field of 13 kV The as-obtained electrospun nanofibers were collected and stored in air overnight.

nodes.name: Calcination of electrospun nanofibers
nodes.procedure: The as-obtained electrospun nanofibers were transferred into a tube furnace for calcination. Then, the temperature of the tube furnace was raised at a ramp rate of 3°C min⁻¹ in air and maintained at the target temperature for 6 h. After naturally cooling down, the black products were collected and named as IrOₓ/Y₂O₃-y, where y represented the treated temperature.

nodes.name: Chemical etching in H₂SO₄
nodes.procedure: The catalytic IrOₓ/Y₂O₃ electrodes were submerged into 0.5 M H₂SO₄ for 10 min. The resulting electrocatalysts were indexed as IrOₓ/Y₂O₃-C, where 'C' represented the chemical etching.
nodes.source_text: For the acidic chemical etching experiments, the catalytic IrOₓ/Y₂O₃ electrodes were submerged into 0.5 M H₂SO₄ for 10 min

nodes.name: Electrochemical etching in H₂SO₄
nodes.procedure: The pristine electrodes were subjected to various consecutive linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) cycles in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ (potential window of 1.04 - 1.74 V versus RHE at a scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹). The etched electrocatalysts were named as IrOₓ/Y₂O₃-EC, in which 'EC' represented the electrochemical etching.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows exposed facets (222) plane and (110) plane with d spacings of 0.306 nm and 0.318 nm for Y2O3 and IrO2 respectively in IrOx/Y2O3.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS determines actual Ir/Y molar ratio of 5.8:4.2 for IrOx/Y2O3 catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Determined by ICP-MS, the actual Ir/Y molar ratio of as-synthesized IrOx/Y2O3 catalysts was 5.8:4.2.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM X-ray mappings show uniform distribution of Ir and Y in IrOx/Y2O3 nanotubes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HAADF-STEM X-ray mappings of IrOx/Y2O3 nanotubes indicated the co-existence and uniform distribution of Ir and Y in the catalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of IrOx/Y2O3 indexed to rutile phase IrO2; spent IrOx/Y2O3-EC also indexed to rutile phase IrO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1b, the XRD pattern of as-synthesized catalysts was indexed to rutile phase IrO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Y-O peak red-shifted to 358 cm⁻¹, Ir-O vibrations at ≈548 and ≈709 cm⁻¹ for IrOx/Y2O3 confirming coexistence of iridium oxide and yttrium oxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In comparison with the Raman profile of Y2O3 alone with a characterized vibration peak of Y-O at 375 cm⁻¹ as-synthesized IrOx/Y2O3 catalysts exhibited a red-shift of that peak at 358 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows pores in nanotube walls of IrOx/Y2O3-EC after electrochemical etching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM characterizations demonstrated the occurrence of the electrochemical etching of IrOx/Y2O3 with the appearance of the pores in the wall of nanotubes.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of IrOx/Y2O3-EC shows 0.224 nm and 0.265 nm lattice fringes corresponding to (200) planes of rutile IrO2 and (400) planes of Y2O3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the electrochemical etching during the acidic OER process, HRTEM images further confirmed that IrOx/Y2O3-EC was composed of numerous tiny IrO2 and Y2O3 nanocrystals with the 0.224 and 0.265 nm lattice fringes corresponding to the (200) planes of rutile IrO2 and the (400) planes of Y2O3 respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental X-ray mapping shows uniform distribution of Y and Ir in IrOx/Y2O3-EC after electrochemical etching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Yttrium and iridium preserved the uniform distribution in the catalysts after the electrochemical acidic etching, as shown in the elemental X-ray mapping images.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance C_DL determined as 3.34 mF for IrOx/Y2O3-EC and 0.85 mF for IrOx/Y2O3, indicating 3.9 times higher ECSA for etched catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The current density differences showed that the double-layer capacitance (C_DL) was a function of the scan rates... As a result, the C_DL of IrOx/Y2O3-EC (3.34 mF) was higher than that of IrOx/Y2O3 (0.85 mF) by a factor of 3.9

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir 4f XPS shows mixture of Ir³⁺ (37.7%) and Ir⁴⁺ in IrOx/Y2O3-EC (increased Ir³⁺ from 33.6% in IrOx/Y2O3); Y 3d confirms Y³⁺ as Y2O3; O 1s shows increased oxygen vacancy from 20.5% to 38.8%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the pre-electrochemical etching, the fraction of Ir³⁺ on the catalyst surface increased from the initial value of 33.6% in IrOx/Y2O3 to that of 37.7% in IrOx/Y2O3-EC. The peak area percentages of OV greatly increased from 20.5% in IrOx/Y2O3 to 38.8% in IrOx/Y2O3-EC.
